html:
SMTO-CAP-0008 — A Skill or tool is set to both use and never use

GUID: 7bd66a90-49d7-429b-8b33-03b75936ea84
Slug: capability-preference-conflict
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • Your capability choices both favor and block the same Skill or tool, or favor a tool whose whole Skill is blocked. SMTO can't follow both, so it didn't accept these choices.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Capabilities by the message box and type the Skill or tool named in the message into the search box. The message lists exactly which item has the two opposite choices.
  2. Choose one setting for it: Always or + Prefer to favor it, or Never or − Exclude to block it. Picking one setting replaces any other rule for that item, which removes the contradiction.
  3. If the message says a preferred tool belongs to an excluded Skill, set that Skill back to Auto or ○ Enable, or stop favoring the tool. Then select Apply. A tool can't be favored while the Skill it belongs to is blocked.

What success looks like

  • Apply closes the Capabilities window without an error, and your next request starts normally.

If it still fails

  • Check the same item under each Apply to choice (This prompt, This conversation, Global), because each keeps its own rules. If it still fails, send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep applying the same choices; they are rejected until one rule changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability policy validation found the same identity in both a preferred_* and an excluded_* list (Preferred/excluded conflict), or normalize_policy found a preferred tool owned by an excluded Skill.

What this means

  • Canonical policy validation found overlap between preferred and excluded tools/skills, including a preferred tool inside an excluded skill. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Canonical policy validation found overlap between preferred and excluded tools/skills, including a preferred tool inside an excluded skill.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare direct preference/exclusion lists and inherited skill exclusions; inspect the specific overlapping identity.

How to fix it

  • Read the overlapping IDs from the message and remove one side in the affected scope's policy (prompt, conversation or global); see AgentCapabilityPolicy.canonical_lists and normalize_policy in src/agent_runtime/capability_policy.py. Re-validate with POST /api/agent/capabilities/validate before saving, and don't widen the enabled sets to resolve it.
  • Review the selected preferences and exclusions. Remove the contradiction without enabling capabilities beyond the intended scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The canonical policy contains no preferred item excluded directly or through its skill.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
